Today's read · our judgment, with the receipts

The Iran deal is dead — and the market stopped pretending otherwise.

The May 31 deadline passed unsigned, peace odds collapsed to 4%, and Ukraine widened the war the same night. We read this as escalation, not noise — here's why, and where we could be wrong.

Corroboration
6 sources · 4 sections

Polymarket's US–Iran peace deal by May 311 prints at 4%, down from 8% a week ago, and the Hormuz blockade-lifting contract fell from 33% to 18% in 48 hours1. The market has, in effect, stopped pricing a deal. In the same window Ukraine's SBU destroyed two Tu-142 aircraft and an Iskander system at Taganrog2 and struck the Feodosiya oil terminal in Crimea.

What deserves attention is the shape of the response: fresh OFAC Counter-Terrorism Designations3 and an amended Iran FAQ point to an administration hardening its floor to denuclearization. The ceasefire was never formally extended4 — but it was never formally broken either, which is exactly where our read is most exposed.

Why it matters

Energy and escalation risk repriced together — rare, and usually a leading indicator.

Where we're exposed

If the ceasefire quietly holds, "rupture" is an over-read. We're tracking the OFAC text for a 72h reversal.
